description.narrative: The primary objective of the project is to establish and install an appropriate set of regional payment mechanisms to satisfy the evolving needs of all market sectors in the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) - consumercomma retailcomma industrialcomma commerc ialcomma governmentcomma financial marketscomma and international - for making payments in a safecomma soundcomma secure and timely manner with certainty and at an acceptable cost. A secondarycomma but nevertheless equally important objectivecomma is that the new payments systems satisfy internationally accepted standards and core principles and thus ensure a high level of user confidence in the WAEMU financial systems. A well-functioning paymentscomma clearing and settlement system is key to an efficient financial sectorcomma and plays an important role in reducing creditcomma liquidity and systemic risks in the system. By supporting the implementation of a state-of-the-art payment system for the entire WAEMU regioncomma the project would contribute to the development of non-cash transactionscomma the strengthening of bankscomma the deepening of the financial sectorcomma andcomma more generallycomma increased regional integration and the expansion of trade and investment among and within member countries. To achieve these objectivescomma the project has five components: (i) project support; (ii) a real time gross settlement system (RTGScomma renamed STAR-UEMOA: Système de Transfert Automatisé et de Règlement); (iii) a low value clearing system (COMPENS)comma renamed SICA: Système Interbancaire de Compensation Automatisé); (iv) an inter-bank card system; and (v) a common telecommunications and computer infrastructure based on BCEAO's facilities. (i) global project support which includes developing the legal framework and administrative support; (ii) The RTGS component includes the establishment of a RTGS at the regional level which would be open to banks and other financial instruments. (iii) The low value clearing component would upgrade existing systems at the national and regional levels to make them more efficient. It will be designed to meet the daily low-value payment needs of a braod spectrum of users and will cover a variety of payment instruments (checkscomma automatic debits and creditscomma payment orderscomma card paymentscomma etc) (iv) The inter-bank card system would develop a common bank card productcomma enabling any bank customer to use it at any automatic teller machine (ATM) or participating merchant's facility (point of sale - POS) in the sub-region (v) For all three payment systemscomma the BCEAO telecommunications satellite network would be used to effect transactions with a high degree of security and at a low cost. Local networks would have to be built and secured for connecting banks' local branches and ATM and POS facilities.
